title: Tech Note: Mirroring in version 2004
author: Kent Wilbur, Manager Information Systems, 4D, Inc.
featured_technology: 4D 2004.3 mirroring commands (New log file, INTEGRATE LOG FILE)
Log file / segmented log file transfer

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces two new 4D 2004.3 language commands for building a database mirroring system — periodically closing/segmenting the log file and integrating transferred segments into a standby mirror server — and demonstrates transferring log segments using 4D SOAP calls along with XML-based preference storage. The fundamental log-file-based mirroring concept remains part of 4D Server's architecture, but this note's DIY approach (custom SOAP transfer, manual segment management) predates any later built-in, more automated high-availability/mirroring features 4D introduced, and 4D SOAP itself reflects the SOAP-era web services approach that has since given way to REST-based integration, making the specific implementation techniques here largely superseded even though database mirroring as a concept endures.
related_updates: 4D's database engine and server products have continued to evolve their backup/mirroring/high-availability capabilities well beyond this manual 2004.3-era approach
4D SOAP-based integration has been superseded by REST/HTTP-based approaches in modern 4D web services
Preference/configuration storage in 4D has largely shifted toward JSON rather than hand-built XML
